static_review: WG128 with required SIMD16 has eight subgroups. h=subgroup and h=subgroup+8 owns every one of sixteen real/padded head rows once; the loop count is uniform within every subgroup.
For each h, lane l stores dense16 P tile indices h*16+l and 256+h*16+l. Across sixteen h and sixteen lanes these are exactly the 512 original probability elements with no duplicate writer.

Every lane participates in invalid/max/sum reductions and broadcast with identical operation/source lane. Only lane0 accesses persistent per-head max, alpha, normalizer and diagnostic writes inside the row loop.

The existing WG barriers before softmax and before PV establish score visibility and P/state visibility. Subgroup collectives are not used as local-memory fences. The existing end-of-PV barrier protects the next tile state.
Both probability contributions stay FP32 through the sum; each value is separately rounded into BF16 P for PV. Only FP32 sum association differs; max/alpha/normalizer/accumulator remain FP32.

All-missing or invalid-width paths retain norm=0 and zero output; empty tiles after valid tiles retain prior max and norm. Invalid live Q/K/V diagnostics remain part of the unchanged fixture. These are source observations awaiting execution.
Kernel has no new host arithmetic, scratch allocation, queue synchronization, global copy, or WG barrier. Added collective/broadcast instructions may cost more than saved serial work; no speed claim.
